correctness.rationale: The upper bound orients the size-n part towards both other parts and the size-2 part towards the size-m part; every reachable set has ≤m+3 vertices. For a core obstruction on s-1 colors, the paired-level preference rankings force the i-th level to use colors ≥i, and core vertices to avoid all q lower colors, using actual neighbor witnesses and improperness/2-cycle dichotomy. A stable coloring would contradict the core obstruction. The explicit six-vertex core obstruction has a complete 96-coloring checker with 92 directed 2-cycles and four directed 3-cycles. Additional exhaustive constructed-profile checks at m=3,4 yield 2,940 and 165,360 obstructed assignments; only the quantified proof establishes all m and n. The paper definitions, quantifiers, named-color conventions and boundary m=2 were checked.

value.rationale: The result closes the entire sharp reachability gap for a natural two-parameter class of complete tripartite graphs with arbitrarily large parts. Its paired-level obstruction amplification is a reusable structural principle for preference-stable coloring, not a single tiny instance or a routine use of the reachability upper theorem. The new cases m≥4 grow unboundedly, despite m=2,3 being known from independent earlier results; that precise parameter distinction is documented.
